about: How every SCE engine writes a string into JSON text, written out by hand.
One form, the one the C++ core's nlohmann writer already produces for
`error.communication` data and for script values: `"` and `\` escaped,
the five short forms `\b \f \n \r \t`, every other U+0000-U+001F as
`\u00xx` with lowercase hex, and everything else - U+007F and all
non-ASCII - written as it is, in UTF-8. RFC 8259 permits other spellings;
SCE allows exactly one, so the same value is the same bytes whichever
engine wrote it, and a document or a peer cannot tell them apart.
Why a shared table: measured 2026-09-28, eleven hand-written escapers
across six engines agreed on none of the control characters - five
passed U+0001 through raw, which is not JSON at all - and no test pinned
any of them, because each engine's tests were written against that
engine. A table read by all of them is the only thing that holds them
Each case gives `text` (read with the reading engine's own JSON parser)
and `escaped`, the body its writer must produce, without the quotes.
The rule is stated once, in ARCHITECTURE.md, 'JSON Text (Single Source
of Truth)', which lists the readers.
